scenarios.trigger: an operator or application deletes or corrupts a bounded logical set
scenarios.preferred_evidence: audit trail, transaction time or named restore point
scenarios.primary_method: isolated PITR followed by comparison or selective logical export
scenarios.rto_driver: restore, replay, validation and controlled data merge

scenarios.trigger: all database copies in one storage or failure domain are unavailable
scenarios.preferred_evidence: repository inventory, latest complete backup and WAL range
scenarios.rto_driver: provisioning, bytes restored, WAL replay and service cutover

scenarios.trigger: database, control plane and local backup repository are lost together
scenarios.primary_method: restore in a separate region or promote a designed DR system
scenarios.rto_driver: regional capacity, dependencies, routing and business validation

scenarios.trigger: records must remain recoverable or provably deleted for a policy period
scenarios.preferred_evidence: retention policy, legal hold, object immutability and restore tests
scenarios.rto_driver: catalog search, key access and restore procedure

non_substitutes: a streaming replica is not an independent backup because logical mistakes replay
a successful backup command is not proof that a restore can start and satisfy business invariants
a storage snapshot is not transactionally useful unless its consistency and WAL relationship are designed
a logical dump cannot be inserted into a physical WAL replay chain
